A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CommonLID study. Their text, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocated and renumbered sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of language-identification systems and GPT models, dataset statistics, and inference-speed measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds annotation-disagreement statistics and examples of GlotLID errors.

M1.justification: The CommonLID collection, annotation and cleaning procedures remain unchanged, as do model inference and label normalization. The added agreement analysis examines existing annotations without establishing a change to dataset construction or model procedures.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 109-language CommonLID benchmark alongside FLORES+, SmolSent, UDHR-LID, Bibles and social-media data. The new agreement analysis and error examples use existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same eight LID systems and four GPT variants. Comparator membership in Tables 1–3 and the appendix inference-speed comparison is unchanged.

E3.justification: New Section 4.2 introduces an agreement-analysis protocol using 67,625 multiply annotated lines after short-span filtering but before other quality filters, followed by inspection of conflicting labels. Existing benchmark sampling, preprocessing, metrics and the 15,000-sample LLM comparison remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing manual cleaning and per-language audit, v2 analyzes whether annotation disagreements reflect mistakes or linguistic ambiguity. Appendix C also adds ten illustrative GlotLID misclassifications in Table 5. These are targeted additions to data-quality and error analysis.

E5.justification: v2 first reports estimated annotation-disagreement rates, including an adjustment excluding mislabeled English boilerplate. v1 stated that an agreement study was impossible. No model-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests are newly reported.

E6.justification: All seven tables retained from v1 have unchanged values. v2 newly reports 2,137 conflicting-label lines out of 67,625 (3.2%), an adjusted 1,524 (2.3%), and ten error examples. Its two-label subgroup counts—1,218, 658 and 254—sum to 2,130, conflicting with the stated total of 2,043.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, theorems or proofs are added or revised. The added sampling arithmetic and disagreement percentages are descriptive calculations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a community-annotated multilingual web benchmark, comparative LID evaluations, and evidence that existing evaluations overestimate web-domain accuracy. The added validation does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v1's statement that agreement analysis was impossible becomes a limitation on conducting a full study. v2 interprets the partial analysis through boilerplate mistakes and ambiguous language boundaries, particularly the Arabic continuum, and judges the adjusted disagreement reasonable. Other principal interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Dataset and evaluation-code footnotes change from publication placeholders to explicit Hugging Face and GitHub access locations. v2 also identifies the processing stage used for its agreement statistics. Existing implementation and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The SmolSent appendix attribution changes from Caswell et al. (2020) to the distinct SMOL paper, Caswell et al. (2025). Section 2.1 also stops characterizing unavailable training data as proprietary. These are limited attribution and positioning refinements; the reference list is unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative order are retained. Changes include a revised recruitment paragraph, small wording corrections, updated affiliations, a new agreement subsection and error-example appendix, and relocation of full affiliations to Appendix A.

P2.justification: v2 adds the error-example table and enlarges model labels in Figure 2. Moving full affiliations to the appendix brings the abstract and introduction onto page 1. Existing tables and figures are retained with relocation, reflow and limited screenshot resizing.

improvement.justification: Explicit dataset/code access locations, partial agreement analysis and concrete error examples improve reproducibility and scrutiny of the unchanged benchmark study. The gains are limited: agreement analysis covers only a subset, and its inconsistent two-label counts reduce confidence in the detailed breakdown.
